subject: Re: Project Saffron — bake-off results + a trade-off
body:
Bake-off numbers are in for Saffron.

On our long-tail slice (90 languages), 10.7b-mt beats 7b-mt by +1.8 chrF on average, but 7b-mt-bt — the backtranslation-finetuned checkpoint — closes to within 0.4 chrF of the 10.7B on the lowest-resource third while being materially cheaper to serve. The 3b-mt is fine as a fallback tier only.

Trade-off for the launch review: serve 7b-mt-bt as primary and accept the 0.4 chrF gap, or serve 10.7b-mt and eat roughly 40% higher serving cost at the latency target Milan measured post-quantization. My recommendation is 7b-mt-bt primary, 10.7B behind a quality-critical flag.

One risk: a handful of low-resource languages show audit artifacts inherited from the web crawl; Yara is compiling the exclusion list so we don't demo those at LRB.

Carmen
